messages:

Subject: Re: Intro + demo — follow-up and pilot ask

Thanks for the demo today, Dylan — good, pragmatic conversation. Quick recap from our side and the things we'll need to evaluate before procurement signs off: 

- Primary asks:
  - We want an apples-to-apples comparison against the hyperscaler (our baseline runs on CloudX reserved GPUs) for our 512-token generative model (decoder-only). Key metrics: p50/p95/p99 token latency, sustained throughput (QPS/tokens per second) for 48h, and unit cost per 1M tokens at our observed batching patterns.
  - Cold-start behavior on burst traffic (how prewarming / pool scaling works).
  - Fallback behavior: if dedicated pool saturates, how quickly and gracefully do you failover to compatible hosted variants?
  - Reservation/commit path: what are the minimum reservation terms to guarantee the capacity we need, and how does pricing move with a 12m commit?

- Next tests we can run from our side: provide payloads and a small synthetic traffic generator. We can run your supplied harness and our own.

I've attached the procurement template and the mutual action plan stub (brightline-mop-v1.xlsx). Priya (procurement) will need a simple pilot statement of work with dates and guarantees. We need to see concrete numbers to compare to CloudX's reserved instance effective cost.

Can Redwood run a 7-day dedicated pilot on a small reserved pool + a hosted fallback, capture the metrics above, and provide the logs (token-level latency distributions + cost breakdown) for review?

Thanks,
Samir Rao
Head of Platform Engineering
Brightline Labs

From: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai

Subject: Fwd: Intro + demo — follow-up and pilot ask (Brightline)

Forwarding Samir's note — Brightline wants a bounded pilot that directly compares our Dedicated reservations to their CloudX reserved baseline. Key asks: p50/p95/p99 latencies for a 512-token workload, sustained 48h throughput, cold-start/burst behavior, and a fallback path to hosted variants. Procurement (Priya) wants a short SOW and dates.

Proposed test matrix (my recommendation):
1) Latency sweep: 512-token generation, sequence-length distribution sampled from their payloads, run 1 thread-level test for 30m at increasing offered QPS (10, 50, 100) measuring p50/p95/p99 and per-token cost.
2) Sustained run: 48h sustained workload at their expected average QPS (they indicated ~120 QPS peak, will confirm) to surface drift/thermal throttling and effective unit cost.
3) Cold-start bursts: simulate 0->burst from 10->200 QPS to validate prewarm/autoscale and measure 0-10s tail latency behavior.
4) Fallback verification: deliberately saturate dedicated pool and validate automated routing to hosted variant, measure failover time and any QoS degradation.

Action items: aditya — can you pull the latest benchmark summary (kernel selection notes + quantization profiles) and the short runbook we can hand to Brightline's engs? laura — can you draft a 7-day pilot SOW (start/end dates TBD) with one-week reservation of 1x A100-80GB equiv pool and a hosted fallback SLA? Also include a simple liability/acceptance clause for the pilot.

I'll coordinate scheduling and get the test harness to them. We should capture token-level traces and a lightweight dashboard (p95/p99 time-series + cost).

Thanks,
Dylan
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

On 12/12/2026 4:05 PM, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai wrote:
> Forwarding Samir's note — Brightline wants a bounded pilot that directly compares our Dedicated reservations to their CloudX reserved baseline.

Thanks — attaching the current benchmark package and a short test harness we use for customer pilots. Notes: 
- Attached: redwood-benchmark-summary-4p.zip (includes kernel selection notes, sequence-length profiles, and a lightweight harness script).
- For a fair comparison we should match model quantization and batch-size distributions; I'll include recommended config snapshots (fp16 + 4-bit quant qual variants) in the Drive link as well.
- Reservation sizing: 1x A100-80GB equiv pool is a reasonable starting point for their stated traffic; if they want headroom for spikes we can recommend 1.5x for the pilot but that raises cost.
- Fallback plan: we recommend using a model-variant fallback combined with route-level throttling: when dedicated pool >=85% sustained, route new sessions to hosted compatible variant (same family, slightly lower perf). That yields near-zero error rates and predictable degradation. We can instrument failover with a 5s warmup window to avoid cold-cache penalties.

I'll ask infra to earmark capacity for next week (we need approvals from capacity ops). Laura — happy to pair on the SOW; I'll add a short SLA clause that we meet 99.5% availability during the pilot for the reserved pool and provide the telemetry artifacts.

Attachments: redwood-benchmark-summary-4p.zip

- Aditya

What we'll deliver (pilot scope):
- 7-day dedicated pilot (Mon–Sun), reserved pool: 1x A100-80GB equiv for Brightline's traffic profile. Hosted fallback enabled and instrumented.
- Data we will provide: token-level latency distributions (p50/p95/p99), time-series of throughput, CPU/GPU utilization, and a per-token cost breakdown for the duration of the pilot.
- Tests to run: latency sweep (512-token workload), 48h sustained run, cold-start burst scenarios, failover verification.
- Acceptance: Brightline will sign the mutual action plan and confirm start date. At pilot completion we will deliver the benchmark artifact bundle and a short readout session.

Timeline & next steps:
1) Priya: if procurement can sign the attached MOP and the one-page SOW (I've attached a draft mip_brightline_draft.pdf), we can kick off pilot the week of 2026-12-21 pending infra capacity approval.
2) Laura/laura_bennett@redwood.ai will schedule a 30m kickoff to finalize telemetry hooks and test payload delivery.
3) Aditya will drop the benchmark zip and the harness into the shared Drive link for Brightline to run locally if they want parallel runs.

Attachments: mip_brightline_draft.pdf (one-page SOW), redwood-benchmark-summary-4p.zip

Let me know if you want the pilot shortened or adjusted. We're prepared to provide a pricing quote for a 12-month reservation after the pilot if the numbers look favorable.
